item.title: Fiji deports fugitive wanted in India over investment fraud
item.description: A man wanted in India over an alleged investment fraud involving the equivalent of about $555,000 has been deported from Fiji following a joint operation involving Indian authorities and Fijian officials. According to India’s Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Rahul Shamrao Kalokhe was deported on Thursday after being located in Fiji through an Interpol Red Notice.
item.content:encoded:
A man wanted in India over an alleged investment fraud involving the equivalent of about $555,000 has been deported from Fiji following a joint operation involving Indian authorities and Fijian officials.

According to India’s Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Rahul Shamrao Kalokhe was deported on Thursday after being located in Fiji through an Interpol Red Notice.

Indian authorities allege Kalokhe cheated a businessman in the city of Pune by promising monthly investment returns of between 6 and 8 per cent through stock market investments.

The alleged fraud involved Rs23.8 million, equivalent to approximately $555,000 at current exchange rates.

Pune City Police registered a cheating case against Kalokhe in 2025, while a second cheating case has also been filed against him by police in Ahilyanagar.

The CBI said Kalokhe fled India to evade investigation and legal proceedings.

Following a request from Maharashtra Police, the CBI secured an Interpol Red Notice, which enabled authorities to trace and arrest him in Fiji.

After completing the required legal processes, Kalokhe was deported to India, where he arrived on 30 July accompanied by an escort team from Indian law enforcement.

item.title: Only three in ten HIV cases diagnosed in Fiji
item.description: Only about three in every 10 people estimated to be living with HIV in Fiji have been diagnosed, highlighting the scale of the country’s rapidly growing HIV outbreak, health officials have revealed. item.content:encoded:
Only about three in every 10 people estimated to be living with HIV in Fiji have been diagnosed, highlighting the scale of the country’s rapidly growing HIV outbreak, health officials have revealed.

Speaking at the 26th International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) in Rio de Janeiro, Chair of Fiji’s National HIV Outbreak and Cluster Response Taskforce, Dr Jason Mitchell, said Fiji is facing the fastest-growing HIV epidemic in the world and requires sustained international support.

National surveillance data shows that only about 30 per cent of estimated HIV cases have been diagnosed, while around one in six people living with HIV are receiving treatment. Documented viral suppression stands at just two per cent.

Since declaring a national HIV outbreak in January 2025, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services has recorded a 14-fold increase in new HIV diagnoses over the past five years.

According to UNAIDS estimates, 1.6 per cent of Fiji’s adult population—about one in every 60 adults—is now living with HIV. The agency has also increased its estimate of people living with HIV in Fiji from 8,900 in 2025 to 12,000 in 2026, indicating transmission is exceeding previous projections.

Dr Mitchell said the outbreak is being driven largely by injecting methamphetamine use, with two-thirds of new diagnoses over the past year involving people aged 20 to 34.

While Fiji has expanded access to pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), peer outreach, condom distribution and integrated primary healthcare, Dr Mitchell said the country still lacks a large-scale needle and syringe programme to reduce transmission through contaminated injecting equipment.

“Fiji is currently navigating the fastest-growing HIV epidemic in the world,” Dr Mitchell said.

He warned that Fiji’s experience should serve as an early warning for other Pacific Island countries facing similar challenges and called on the international community to continue supporting small island developing states.

“This is not a Fiji problem alone, it’s an early warning for the entire region. We are calling on the global community not to turn its back on small island developing states who stand to lose so much if we don’t respond fast and strong,” he said.

item.title: Goundar Shipping praises crew after sea rescue
item.description: Goundar Shipping Limited has commended the captain and crew of the Lomaiviti Princess 12 for their role in the successful search and rescue of six missing medical personnel at sea. In a statement, GSL Management paid tribute to Captain, person referred as Drick and his crew, describing their actions as courageous, professional and driven by a strong commitment to saving lives.
item.content:encoded:
Goundar Shipping Limited has commended the captain and crew of the Lomaiviti Princess 12 for their role in the successful search and rescue of six missing medical personnel at sea.

In a statement, GSL Management paid tribute to Captain, person referred as Drick and his crew, describing their actions as courageous, professional and driven by a strong commitment to saving lives.

The company also thanked God for His protection and guidance throughout the rescue operation, saying faith played an important role during the challenging mission.

Following the rescue, the Lomaiviti Princess 12 continued its voyage to Lakeba to ensure the rescued medical personnel received the necessary care before proceeding to Oneata later in the evening.

Goundar Shipping also acknowledged the patience and understanding of passengers aboard the vessel, saying their cooperation allowed the captain and crew to focus fully on the emergency operation.

The company praised everyone involved, saying the crew’s bravery, teamwork and willingness to respond in a time of need reflected the true spirit of service, compassion and responsibility.

GSL concluded by wishing God’s continued protection over its seafarers, passengers and all those travelling on Fiji’s waters.

item.title: Burnt cane deliveries hampering sugar production, says FSC
item.description: The Fiji Sugar Corporation is urging cane growers to stop burning sugarcane, warning that high volumes of burnt cane are reducing sugar recovery, increasing production costs and placing additional pressure on mill operations. In a statement, FSC said that as of 7:00am on 29 July, burnt cane accounted for 20 per cent of all cane delivered nationally since the start of the 2026 crushing season. Over
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Sugar Corporation is urging cane growers to stop burning sugarcane, warning that high volumes of burnt cane are reducing sugar recovery, increasing production costs and placing additional pressure on mill operations.

In a statement, FSC said that as of 7:00am on 29 July, burnt cane accounted for 20 per cent of all cane delivered nationally since the start of the 2026 crushing season. Over the previous 24 hours, 55 per cent of cane delivered to Rarawai Mill, 44 per cent to Lautoka Mill and 12 per cent to Labasa Mill had been burnt prior to harvest.

FSC said burnt cane deteriorates rapidly after harvesting, reducing its natural sugar content and resulting in lower sugar extraction during milling.

The Corporation said burnt cane also contains more impurities, requiring additional chemicals and more intensive processing to maintain sugar quality. It said this accelerates wear on factory equipment, reduces factory throughput and increases operating and maintenance costs.

FSC said it continues to invest heavily in improving mill reliability and operational efficiency, but those efforts are undermined when excessive volumes of burnt cane are delivered for processing.

The Corporation is encouraging growers to harvest green cane wherever practical and deliver it to mills as quickly as possible, saying this would improve sugar recovery, lower processing costs and support a more sustainable sugar industry.

FSC also acknowledged growers who continue to deliver fresh, high-quality cane and called for the continued cooperation of all industry stakeholders to improve cane quality throughout the remainder of the 2026 crushing season.

item.title: Six missing healthcare workers found safe at sea
item.description: The Fiji Navy has confirmed that the six people reported missing at sea in the Lau Group have been found safe, bringing a successful end to a major search and rescue operation. In a statement, the Navy said the six were located about 11 nautical miles southwest of Lakeba by the Goundar Shipping vessel Lomaiviti Princess 12 .
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Navy has confirmed that the six people reported missing at sea in the Lau Group have been found safe, bringing a successful end to a major search and rescue operation.

In a statement, the Navy said the six were located about 11 nautical miles southwest of Lakeba by the Goundar Shipping vessel Lomaiviti Princess 12 .

The Navy thanked mariners and vessels operating in the area for responding quickly to the search effort, with special acknowledgement given to the captain and crew of Lomaiviti Princess 12 for locating and rescuing the missing group.

It also acknowledged the efforts of government agencies, search teams, communities and individuals who worked together during the operation.

The Navy said the successful rescue highlighted the importance of cooperation and vigilance among government agencies and the maritime community.

The six healthcare workers had been reported missing while travelling from Moce to Oneata on a Ministry of Health outreach mission after their vessel developed engine problems and began taking on water.

item.title: Diabetes Fiji calls for national NCD response
item.description: Diabetes Fiji has called for an urgent nationwide response after new health data revealed diabetes and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are reaching unprecedented levels across the country. Speaking on the findings of the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey, Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the latest figures should serve as a wake-up call for government, businesses, civil society, sp
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes Fiji has called for an urgent nationwide response after new health data revealed diabetes and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are reaching unprecedented levels across the country.

Speaking on the findings of the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey, Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the latest figures should serve as a wake-up call for government, businesses, civil society, sporting organisations and faith-based groups.

“In light of alarming epidemiological findings from the recent 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey, Diabetes Fiji is issuing an urgent clarion call to government bodies, corporate entities, civil society organisations, sports federations, and faith-based institutions to forge a united front against the nation’s non-communicable disease (NCD) epidemic,” Mr Marawa said.

The survey found diabetes prevalence had climbed to between 16.5 and 17 per cent, up from 14.6 per cent in 2011.

It also showed 98.5 per cent of adults aged 18 to 69 have at least one risk factor for NCDs, while 47 per cent live with three or more risk factors.

“Over 68 per cent of adults are classified as overweight or obese, with obesity affecting 40 per cent of the population, 70 per cent of whom are women.”

Mr Marawa said the survey also found 36.6 per cent of Fijians had hypertension, with almost half previously unaware they had the condition.

“Crucially, only 21 per cent consume the recommended daily intake of fruits and vegetables.”

“While 30 per cent smoke, 49 per cent consume alcohol and 56 per cent drink kava and they are predominantly males.”

Mr Marawa said the findings underscored the need for a coordinated national effort to reverse the growing NCD epidemic.

item.title: NCD Crisis | Marawa: Diabetes no longer age-related
item.description: Diabetes is increasingly affecting younger Fijians, with cases now being diagnosed in children as young as one year and seven months, according to the latest findings highlighted by Diabetes Fiji. Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey showed the disease was no longer confined to older age groups.
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes is increasingly affecting younger Fijians, with cases now being diagnosed in children as young as one year and seven months, according to the latest findings highlighted by Diabetes Fiji.

Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey showed the disease was no longer confined to older age groups.

“4.7 per cent of young adults aged 18-29 years now live with diabetes,” Mr Marawa said.

“Tragically, the youngest diagnosed cases with Type 1 diabetes stand at one year and seven months, 11 years old with Type 2, and a stroke recorded in a 12-year-old.”

He said the findings also exposed significant gaps in diagnosis and treatment.

“Among those living with diabetes, only 46.5 per cent are aware of their condition, a mere 33 per cent to 71 per cent receive medical treatment a critically low 6.2 per cent to 21.5 per cent achieve optimal blood glucose control.”

He said the consequences were devastating, with non-communicable diseases responsible for 80 per cent of all deaths in Fiji and between 30 and 40 per cent classified as premature deaths among adults aged 35 to 55.

“Diabetes is also the root cause of 68.5 per cent of end-stage kidney failure cases and 27 per cent of sight-threatening diabetic retinopathy.

Mr Marawa said the survey further found an amputation is performed every 8.5 hours, while 45 per cent of cardiac admissions were linked to life-threatening heart attacks, contributing to seven deaths every day.

item.title: NCD fight ‘overlooked’
item.description: Diabetes Fiji has criticised the Government’s funding priorities, claiming the country’s biggest public health crisis continues to be overlooked despite repeated calls for greater investment in the fight against non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Executive officer Kini Marawa said the organisation was disappointed that its budget submissions and requests for financial assistance had failed to secur
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes Fiji has criticised the Government’s funding priorities, claiming the country’s biggest public health crisis continues to be overlooked despite repeated calls for greater investment in the fight against non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

Executive officer Kini Marawa said the organisation was disappointed that its budget submissions and requests for financial assistance had failed to secure dedicated government funding.

“Diabetes Fiji expresses profound disappointment in the current policy trajectory, which continues to relegate NCDs – our nation’s greatest public health crisis – to a secondary concern,” Mr Marawa said.

“Despite our relentless advocacy, active participation in national budget consultations, and submission of comprehensive, data-driven budget proposals year after year – including throughout the recent financial year – our requests for dedicated financial support have continuously been overlooked and left unaddressed by the government.”

Mr Marawa questioned the Government’s priorities, arguing that economic development could not be sustained without a healthy population.

“Why is public health continually treated as a secondary priority when 80 per cent of our mortality is driven by NCDs? Healthcare must be the primary priority, not an afterthought.”

He also expressed concern that no dedicated budget allocation had been provided to civil society organisations supporting the Ministry of Health and Medical Services.

“Diabetes Fiji notes with concern that the government has failed to allocate a dedicated budgetary line to civil society organisations that directly support the Ministry of Health and Medical Services on the frontlines.”

Despite the funding concerns, Mr Marawa said Diabetes Fiji continued to deliver its Primary Healthcare Screening Program with support from corporate partners, donor agencies and the ministries of Health and Women.

He said the organisation’s focus extended beyond community screening to ensuring patients remained connected to treatment and care through close collaboration with the Health Ministry.
